title: Noise-band Intraday Momentum in Nasdaq-100 Futures
abstract: This paper adapts the intraday momentum strategy of Zarattini et al. (2024), which trades breaks from a "noise area" around the open on the SPY ETF, to Nasdaq-100 futures (NQ) at a fixed size of one micro contract and under constraints that permit unattended webhook execution. On one-minute data from 2020 to July 2026 the executable rule earns +$10.26 per trading day net of costs (day-block bootstrap 95% interval [+$3.27, +$17.25]), with a daily Sharpe ratio of 1.14 and positive results in each of seven calendar years, two of them only marginally. The paper reports the degradation at each step from the published specification to the executable one, a lookahead audit of the trailing stop, and execution stress tests showing that one index point of slippage on stop fills removes 22% of the edge. A three-year block bootstrap of drawdown gives a 95th-percentile maximum drawdown of $3,406 as backtested and $4,081 under combined lag and slippage, which determines the minimum account size for deployment. The rule is one of two survivors among 144 preregistered tests on the same archive, all intervals are in-sample, and no live contract has been traded. Pre-registered thresholds for the forward test are stated.
